title: Governed migration runner bootstrap and early-exit diagnostics

phases.objective: Make governed migration runner artifact, module-import, and startup-stage failures observable through bounded redacted diagnostics while preserving the shadow/library-only boundary and without applying migrations, grants, provider mutations, or Production activation.

e2e_journeys.entrypoint: The governed migration execution tool starts the bootstrap wrapper for a dry-run migration request.
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: Artifact and module-import failures produce bounded redacted diagnostics, while valid runner startup reaches stage tracing and remains fail-closed before any database or provider mutation.
steps: Resolve the runner path relative to the tracked bootstrap module.
Check artifact readability before importing the runner.
Capture module-import failures with a stage, bounded message, runner existence flag, and secrets_included=false.
Emit runner startup stages for module load, main entry, argument parsing, authorization preflight, artifact resolution, and schema preflight when those stages are reached.
Run regression tests with missing dependencies or DB configuration so no database connection, migration application, grant, or provider mutation occurs.
Regenerate portable staging and Remote MCP write-scope artifacts only through their official generators.
Keep Production activation, migration apply, DB grants, provider mutation, force push, and secret output disabled.
assertions: Missing runner artifacts fail closed with runner_artifact_readability rather than an unstructured exit.
Import-time failures fail closed with runner_module_import and do not expose secret values or connection strings.
The stage diagnostic path is bounded and reports secrets_included=false.
The execution tool retains child-process timing, output, signal, and diagnostic fields without authorizing execution.
Dry-run regression tests do not require a live database and do not perform SQL or provider mutations.
Generated manifest and inventory artifacts are current according to their official generators.
The environment declaration covers both staging and production because shared runtime code is changed, and requires live staging certification.
No migration, grant, provider mutation, Production deployment, Branch Protection change, Ruleset change, or force push is introduced.
The PR remains bound to its exact candidate SHA and secrets_included=false.
